I've been working this land for 45 years. My plot is small — just 2 mu — and there are only two of us at home now. I know this soil well, and I know what it takes to get a good maize yield out of it.

Quzhou is on the North China Plain. The summers are hot and dry enough that without my well I'd be in trouble. Single-season maize is what I've always done here, and it's what makes sense for a plot this size. I don't have the labor or the water to push a double-crop system anymore.

I'll plant a hybrid — I've used郑单958-type hybrids for years and they perform reliably in this region. Traditional seed is not worth the yield loss. I apply rotary tillage before planting; my plot is too small for a plough and I want to conserve soil moisture.

For fertilizer, I apply base phosphorus and potassium at planting, then split my nitrogen — some at planting, the rest at jointing stage. I've learned from experience not to over-apply nitrogen; it burns money and the crop doesn't use it. 18 kg N/mu is where I've settled after years of trial. I'll apply 6 kg P and 5 kg K.

With well irrigation I'll water 3 times: once before planting to wet the seedbed, once at jointing, and once at tasseling. Those are the critical windows. I don't waste water.

Two pesticide applications — one pre-emergence herbicide and one foliar spray at jointing for corn borer and aphids. I keep it minimal. I know what to watch for.

With good management I expect 650 kg/mu. On 2 mu that's 1,300 kg total — enough for household use and some to sell.
